questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language and level of education

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the pre-arrival process was quite tricky and I felt very much alone in the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I both received help from my accommodation in those matters and from Fiona Hayes and Christopher Sargeant regarding academic issues

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Broadgate Park, Raleigh Park (both self-catered), Jubilee Campus (catered), etc.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a self-catered accommodation (Broadgate Park) and I shared a kitchen with 5 others. It had all the necessary equipment like a stove, microwave, etc. (though not pans, knives, pots, chopping boards, cutlery, etc. - apparently you have to buy those yourself in a lot of the accommodations).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you have to buy all the stuff abovementioned - I went to Ikea on a trip to buy some essential stuff which I had not brought with me. Furthermore, you have to buy bedding as well - also duvets, pillows, etc. If you want to live in Broadgate Park, I highly recommend you not to buy the bedding package - the duvet and pillow is 100% polyester and of terrible quality :O Try and go to a large Tesco (or Ikea) instead, they usually sell duvets and pillows in packages! I also recommend buying a top mattress; the mattress provided is full of springs and not comfortable at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I also recommend putting some effort into making it more homey - eventually, I forgot the surroundings, but I was quite horrified about the apartment at the beginning. It is clean and there is a cleaning service every Wednesday, but it is not at all cozy. I bought some plants and a poster (bought mine during the first week at a Freshers market in front of the Portland building), and also made sure to get some free stuff at the Freshers week.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Basically, I just had to show up and register close to the Portland building during the first few weeks. I had to bring my passport and a lady asked me a couple of questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Fiona and Christopher were both at service whenever we needed help during the first few weeks. Also, I received a lot of information on my Nottingham email, which was a great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise you to not panic about not knowing things. My schedule was announced a couple of days before the semester started, which I found very stressful - but everything worked out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of my courses were on level 3.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is much more engaging, and it is expected of the students that they participate in the discussions. I guess that is the difference between the Danish and English law systems; English law is more dynamic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Tort, Foundations of Criminal Evidence, Classical Legal Theory

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Classical Legal Theory. This course gives you a great understanding of what law is from a philosophical perspective and furthermore prepares you for your next semester (retsfilosofi etc.). It strengthens your analytical skills and gives you a great understanding of different jurisdictions around the world.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds! Please join a society and buy a one-semester membership in David Ross Sports Village if you are in to sports (you can buy that in their reception, it is not available to buy online for only one semester).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend the climbing society. They do loads of socials, and every Wednesday they go climbing and then go to the pub. This was the best way of getting to know English students, as it can be quite hard in other ways to meet with them. I have so many really good friends from Climbing soc!
Also - join the Travel Society! This is a great way to see the UK, and you cannot plan it cheaper yourself.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend you to go travel with the Travel Society. They do both day trips and weekend trips. Furthermore, take a trip to London during the weekend or go watch a football game in Manchester. Nottingham is in the middle of England, which is quite an advantage.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy indeed. English culture is not very distant from Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: As beforementioned, go join a society! This is the easiest way to interact with English students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I struggled the most with the language actually. Even though I speak English fluently, my head could get really exhausted, and I couldn't express myself as deliberately and freely as I am able to in Danish.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: English people are some of the kindest people. I will indeed miss being approached as "my love" and "darling" by the staff in the supermarkets or by the bus driver.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Please ask a student who has been to Nottingham before regarding all the pre-departure stuff; I really struggled with all the planning and could have needed some help in that area. 
2. Join a Society.
3. Go explore the country and use your time abroad as a break from home. Do not stress too much about school; if you study everything, you could choose to do nothing but school. Allow yourself to focus on other things as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the library for studying! I practically lived at Hallward, and that was amazing. All students use the library and then we had lunch together. That was fantastic!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My English has improved A LOT. I have gotten so many amazing international friends. Furthermore, it has opened my eyes regarding working abroad. I feel much more confident and ready to meet new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Time management. There are so many things I wanted to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Remember to enjoy it while it lasts. 3 to 4 months is NOT a long time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
